newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Analysts cautious on Burns Philp shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Analysts cautious on Burns Philp shake-up.

text.p: Burns Philp Ltd's decision to sell its herb and spice business could liven up the company's stock short-term, but long term benefits of the move needed to be clarified, analysts said on Monday.

"Burns Philp are getting rid of debt which is what the market has been waiting to see but, long-term, I'm not so sure getting rid of one of their main assets is such a good idea," said Peter Struk, a dealer at Sydney broker, Reynolds and Co.
Burns Philp earlier announced it would sell its herb and spice business to focus on its yeast activities. The company also announced its managing director, Ian Clack would retire.
The food ingredients group has struggled with its U.S. spice operations in the past few years due to heavy competition, especially from U.S. spice group McCormick & Co Inc.
Burns Philp said the decision followed a review of all the group's operations in conjunction with Boston Consulting Group.
Analysts said the ongoing litigation against Burns Philp as a result of the A$600 million collapse of the Estate Mortgage Trusts would continue to weigh on the company's stock.
"For any significant pick-up you would need a resolution of the Estate Mortgage situation," said Andrew Sekely, a senior dealer at broker, Intersuisse.
Burns Philp is a defendent at the trial after its subsidiary Burns Philp Trustee Co (BPTC) was the Estate Mortgage trustee from 1983 until it went into liquidation during a cash crisis in 1990.
"Clearly there are sweeping changes taking place in the company both at the board level and in terms of rationalisation. The market is looking at this positively," Sekely said.
A Sydney-based analyst told Reuters the move was hard to judge before more details were released by Burns Philp.
"The last major asset Burns Philp sold was BBC Hardware to Howard Smith. In retrospect that deal seems to have only benefited Howard Smith," the analyst said.
Burns Philp sold the hardware retail chain, BBC Hardware to Howard Smith for A$446 million in early 1994, a move which helped fund the group's expansion into the U.S. spice market.
The company said it now intended to sell spice brands Durkee-French, Spice Islands and Tone's, British Pepper and Spice, Euroma and Ostman.
Burns Philp shares closed 11 cents higher at A$1.96.
